 News › News News › Meghalaya school holiday on November 13, 2026: Schools to remain closed for Wangala Festival Meghalaya school holiday on November 13, 2026: Schools to remain closed for Wangala Festival
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 9, 2026, 08:32 IST Wangala Festival in Meghalaya Meghalaya state government has announced a holiday for schools across the state on Friday, November 13, 2026, to mark the Wangala Festival . The announcement has been welcomed by students, teachers and parents, as it gives the school community an opportunity to take part in one of the region's most cherished cultural celebrations.
 The holiday applies to all government and private schools, as well as other educational institutions in the state. Authorities have said the decision is intended to allow students, teachers and staff members to participate in the traditional festivities without disruption to their academic commitments. Regular classes will resume after the holiday, in accordance with the scheduled timetable.
 About the Wangala Festival 
 Wangala, popularly known as the "100 Drums Festival", is among the most significant cultural events of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya in Northeast India. 
 The festival marks the conclusion of the harvesting season and is observed as an expression of gratitude to nature for a successful agricultural cycle.
 Beyond its agricultural significance, the festival reflects the rich heritage, traditions and way of life of the Garo community. It underscores the close relationship between tribal people, the natural environment and farming practices that have sustained them for generations.
 Music, dance and tradition 
 Wangala is widely known for its vibrant cultural performances. Participants from the Garo community, dressed in traditional attire, present folk music, rhythmic drumming and colourful dances. The spectacle attracts visitors and tourists from across the country, and the resonant sound of drums has made the festival one of the most distinctive cultural events in Meghalaya.
 For students, the occasion offers a valuable opportunity to engage with local customs and to appreciate the cultural identity of the region, an experience that complements classroom learning.
 Advisory for students and rarents 
 Students and parents are advised to contact their respective schools for official confirmation of the holiday and details regarding reopening dates. Individual institutions may issue additional instructions based on their academic calendars and internal schedules.
 With the holiday falling on a Friday, families will also enjoy a longer weekend, allowing more time to join community celebrations or spend time together.
 The Wangala Festival remains a proud symbol of Meghalaya's cultural diversity. By declaring a holiday for educational institutions, the state government has reaffirmed its commitment to preserving and promoting the traditions of its indigenous communities, while encouraging younger generations to remain connected to their heritage.
